title: prepublishOnly sanity check: fail fast with actionable error when standard/ is not prepped
definition_of_done: `reference-impl/scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` exists and: (1) walks up from `process.cwd()` to locate the repo root by detecting `standard/package.json`; (2) calls `existsSync` on `<repoRoot>/standard/dist/` and `<repoRoot>/standard/node_modules/`; (3) if either is absent, writes to stderr "ERROR: standard/ is not prepped in this environment.\nRun:  cloverleaf-cli prep-worktree <primaryRoot> <worktreeRoot>\n  OR: (cd ../standard && npm ci && npm run build)" and exits with code 1; (4) if both are present, exits 0 with no output.
`reference-impl/package.json` `prepublishOnly` script is updated to `"node scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs && npm test && npm run build"`, placing the sanity check before the vitest/tsc run.

A regression test is added to `reference-impl/tests/` that: (a) simulates a worktree environment where `standard/dist/` and/or `standard/node_modules/` are absent; (b) spawns `check-standard-prepped.mjs` as a subprocess; (c) asserts the process exits non-zero; (d) asserts stderr contains "standard/ is not prepped" and at least one remediation command.
All pre-existing tests in `reference-impl/tests/` continue to pass.
acceptance_criteria: Running `node scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` from a worktree where `standard/dist/` is absent exits with code 1 and prints to stderr a message containing "ERROR: standard/ is not prepped in this environment." and the two remediation options.
Running `node scripts/check-standard-prepped.mjs` from a correctly prepped environment (both `standard/dist/` and `standard/node_modules/` present) exits 0 and produces no output.

Invoking `npm publish` (or `npm publish --dry-run`) from an unprepped worktree terminates at the sanity-check step before vitest or tsc run, and the operator sees the actionable error message on stderr.

The script resolves the repo root correctly when invoked from any subdirectory within `reference-impl/` (e.g., `reference-impl/scripts/`, `reference-impl/tests/`) by walking up to find `standard/package.json`.
